property_summary: After deployment, the reference version has owner = msg.sender (non-zero), while the buggy version sets owner = address(0), so calling sendTo with msg.sender == owner fails on reference (true) and passes on buggy (false) because the require check uses address(0) which is not msg.sender.

After constructor, the REFERENCE version has owner = msg.sender (address(0xAbc…)), the BUGGY version has owner = address(0). Calling sendTo with msg.sender not the owner (any other address) will revert only in REFERENCE (because owner is a non-zero address), but in BUGGY version the require passes (owner == address(0) != msg.sender) so the transfer succeeds – the concrete scenario checks that after construction, a non-owner address cannot send Ether; the BUGGY version incorrectly allows it.

When the owner is set to the deployer (reference) vs address(0) (modified), calling sendTo with the deployer as msg.sender succeeds in the reference but reverts in the modified version because owner is address(0).
The reference requires the caller to be the owner, while the bug version requires the caller to NOT be the owner; when the owner calls sendTo, the reference succeeds but the bug reverts.
After owner calls sendTo(receiver, 100), the receiver's balance increases by 100 in the reference version but by 0 in the buggy version.
Owner calls sendTo with non-zero amount; reference transfers Ether, second version does not, so reference receiver balance is non-zero and second version receiver balance is zero.

When the non-owner calls sendTo, the reference reverts (requires owner) but the second version sends Ether and succeeds; we test by having a non-owner call sendTo with 1 wei to an address, using try/catch to capture revert status.
Only the owner (address(this)) can call sendTo; a non-owner call must revert in the reference but succeed in the buggy version, causing a balance change that the assertion detects.
Owner calls sendTo with non-owner sender; reference reverts, bug version succeeds, so assertTrue on a try/catch failing in reference and passing in bug.

Only the owner (msg.sender) should be able to send ether; the second version removes the ownership check, so any caller can send ether. The test sends ether from a non-owner and expects the transfer to revert on the reference but succeed on the buggy version.
Call sendTo from a non-owner account: reference reverts, second version does not revert and sends Ether.
